title: The sister who saw first
told: the Janamsakhi tradition of Bebe Nanaki

hook.say: before the story, can i ask? who believed in you before anyone else did?
options: then you’ll know her too. listen.
then this story is for you, and i’m glad you’re here. listen.

steps.line: In Talwandi, young Nanak worried the grown-ups. He gave things away, sat silent for hours, and asked questions nobody could answer.
steps.label: a traditional story

steps.line: His father loved him and worried constantly. But his big sister, Nanaki, watched him differently. She believed in him before there was much to go on.

steps.q: Everyone saw the same boy. What did Nanaki see that the others didn’t?
o: That he’d grow out of it in time
That his strangeness was a gift
That he needed a stricter teacher
steps.why: Love can see what isn’t visible yet. Where others saw a boy wasting time, she saw something holy.

steps.line: Nanaki married and moved to the town of Sultanpur. When her brother was a young man, drifting, she brought him there, and her husband found him work.

steps.q: Soon Nanak would travel far with his friend Mardana. Some tellings say Nanaki gave them something for the road. What?
o: A horse for the long road
steps.why: The rabab, the instrument that carried his songs for decades of travel.

steps.line: Some tellings say that when he set out, Nanaki gave the money for Mardana’s rabab, the instrument that would carry her brother’s songs.
steps.label: one telling

steps.line: Before he left, tradition says, he promised her: whenever you remember me, I’ll come. Years later, at the end of her life, he came.
Some Sikhs call Bebe Nanaki the first Sikh, the first follower of the Guru. She was his sister before she was anything else.

steps.q: Tradition says the boy Nanak was named after his big sister. Where did her name come from?
o: Her mother’s parents’ home, the nanke
A famous saint of the village
steps.why: Tradition says Nanaki was born at her nanke, her mother’s family home, and named for it. Her little brother’s name followed hers.

steps.q: Mardana, who played the rabab beside Nanak for decades, came from which background?
steps.why: Bhai Mardana was a Muslim minstrel, a Mirasi, from Nanak’s own village. Sister and friend, Hindu-born and Muslim: his first circle crossed every line.

say: the sources say little about nanaki’s own inner life, and that’s honest. what they remember is the shape of her love: she saw him first, and she made room for what she saw.
the turning point of his life, the river, happened in sultanpur, because she brought him there. sikhs remember that faith often begins with one person who sees you clearly.

steps.q: From the story, what did Nanaki give that mattered most?
o: Belief, and a place to grow into it
steps.why: The rabab helped. But first she believed, and made room.

today.say: today, send one line to someone who saw you first, before there was much to go on. just: i remember what you did. thank you.
options: then send it before the day ends.
then say it out loud, quietly. love still travels.
